originality.rationale: The first-public 2026-10-01 source concerns the strict-contraction obstruction for smooth generators, not multi-coordinate sharp polyhedral generation. Full accessible scientific texts of three closest published findings were compared by hypotheses and conclusions: one neutral coordinate has optimal polyhedra; arbitrary neutral coordinates have a nonoptimal exponential-sized alphabet; one rotating coordinate has a sharp but dynamically different construction. A non-geometric isomorphism can transfer an abstract m+1 symbol generator to q fixed coordinates, but cannot transfer the piecewise-affine geometry. The checked materials do not imply the present all-q, all-m explicit polyhedral equality. Multiple targeted database and general-literature queries found no dominating geometric result. Residual uncertainty concerns older general coding theorems outside searched literature.
residual_risks: An older general smooth-generator construction for nonergodic products might imply the explicit dimension-independent polyhedral statement under different terminology.
An abstract measurable-space equivalence does cover the Borel count but does not preserve polyhedral geometry; the originality claim must remain about the latter.
The full text of the Hoffman–Rudolph article was not inspected; its abstract is only secondary comparative evidence, not a non-coverage certificate.

value.rationale: The question is motivated by the explicit smooth-generator boundary for neutral toral maps. It resolves a natural all-dimensional exact invariant g_poly for every q>=2,m>=2. The proof compresses the formerly explicit up-to-2^(q+1)-symbol high-dimensional simultaneous-comparison observation to a sharp m+1-cell finite-affine partition (just three cells at multiplier two) using dynamical addressing of q scalar thresholds with one shared bit. This is a structural, reproducible sharp classification in a natural infinite family, not a Borel relabeling or finite numerical exercise.
